ai.title: processFileBlock handles new files with replace blocks
ai.summary: Added logic to `processFileBlock` in `backend/src/process-file-block.ts` to handle new files containing replace blocks. When `requestFile` returns null, the function now parses the new content for diff blocks; if found, it constructs the file content from these blocks and returns it, instead of falling through to the default new file creation.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to write a new file that includes sections saying 'replace this part with that part,' it now builds the file's contents directly from those replace instructions instead of saving the file with the raw replace blocks still in it. This only matters if you're asking for a brand-new file with replace-style instructions; files that already exist or new files without replace blocks behave exactly as before. The improvement is already live in today's version.

ai.title: Add 'faster' to homepage copy
ai.summary: Updated hero text in `web/src/app/page.tsx` to include 'faster' when describing codebase editing. This change applies to both mobile and desktop layouts. No functional or performance changes were made.

eli5.text: The homepage now tells you that editing your codebase and running commands is faster, adding the word 'faster' to the headline. This is only a text change, so you would see the updated wording on the website, but nothing about the product itself works any differently. It is live today.

ai.title: Use stored fingerprint for logged-in CLI users
ai.summary: npm-app/src/client.ts now stores `fingerprintId` on `Client` and initializes it from `user?.fingerprintId ?? await calculateFingerprint()`, replacing the global `fingerprintId` export and `initFingerprint()` in npm-app/src/config.ts. The change fixes logged-in users reusing their stored fingerprint and centralizes credential loading, fingerprint generation, and login actions in `Client`, with authentication.knowledge.md documenting the single-source-of-truth pattern. npm-app/src/fingerprint.ts converts `FINGERPRINTING_INFO` from an async IIFE to `getFingerprintInfo()`, and npm-app/src/index.ts drops the startup `initFingerprint()` promise.

eli5.text: If you're a logged-in CLI user, the assistant now uses your already-stored fingerprint instead of generating a new one each time. This fixes a bug where returning users had their device identity reset on every login, and keeps all login credential handling in one organized place.

You can now ask the assistant to edit a specific part of a file by describing the text you want to replace, and it will find and swap just that section without rewriting the whole file. This works alongside the existing ability to add or rewrite files, so small edits to large files are faster and less error-prone. The feature is live today as part of the latest version of the assistant.
